name: Bangla Calendar Display
author: Md Shorov Abedin

sections.description:
Bangla Calendar Display shows the current Bengali (Bangla) date and time on your WordPress site. Version 1.1.0 introduces a modern, flexible design and an easy‑to‑use settings page so you can control exactly how the calendar looks and behaves.

Features

  • Shows the current Bangla date, weekday and time. You can hide the time or the “ই” suffix on day numbers.
  • Choose between several display templates: simple inline text, modern card, stacked grid or a dual calendar that shows the equivalent Gregorian date alongside the Bangla date.
  • Select which parts to show (time, weekday, date only) and customise colours and font size.
  • Admin settings page in the WordPress Dashboard (found under “Bangla Calendar”) – no coding required.
  • Shortcode attributes allow you to override any option on a per‑use basis:
    [msabcd_bangla_calendar display_view=”modern” color_primary=”#C81A1A” format=”date_weekday”]
  • Fully translation‑ready (Text Domain: bangla-calendar-display) and supports any timezone.

The plugin calculates the Bangla date based on the Gregorian calendar using the official Bangla revised calendar; it adjusts correctly before and after Pohela Boishakh (14 April) and handles Bangla leap years for the month of Falgun.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the bangla-calendar-display folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ menu in WordPress.
  3. Use the [msabcd_bangla_calendar] shortcode in any post or page to display the Bangla calendar.
sections.faq:
How do I use the Bangla Calendar?

Once the plugin is activated, go to Bangla Calendar in your WordPress dashboard and choose your preferred style and colours.

To display the calendar on a post, page or widget area, insert the shortcode:

`

[msabcd_bangla_calendar]
`

You can customise each instance using shortcode attributes:

  • display_view – simple, modern, grid or dual_gregorian
  • format – time_date_weekday, date_weekday, time_date, date_only, time_only
  • show_time – 1 or 0
  • show_suffix – 1 or 0
  • color_primary, color_bg, font_size – override the colours or font size (e.g. color_primary="#FF5722")
  • timezone – override the timezone used

Example:

`

[msabcd_bangla_calendar display_view=”modern” format=”date_weekday” color_primary=”#00a32a”]
`
sections.changelog:
1.0.5

  • Added an admin settings page with fields for time display, suffix control, timezone, date format, view template, primary/background colour and font size.
  • Added multiple display templates: simple, modern card, stacked grid and dual calendar (Bangla + Gregorian).
  • Added format options to show/hide the time and weekday (date only, time only, date + weekday, etc.).
  • Added per‑instance shortcode attributes to override any option from the settings page.
  • Improved Bangla date calculation: correctly adjusts the year and day for dates before Pohela Boishakh (14 April) and adds support for leap years in the month of Falgun.
  • Added translation support via Text Domain: bangla-calendar-display.
  • Added colour picker and font size controls in the settings page.

1.0.0

  • Initial release of Bangla Calendar Display plugin.
